topics.desc: Insert Part Studios, parts, surfaces, curves, sketches, planes, active sheet metal models, or mate connectors from one Part Studio into another in the same or a different document (thereby linking the documents), with an associative link. You also have the ability to insert these entities into a Part Studio from a different version of the same document.

topics.title: Variable
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Variable
topics.desc: Create a variable for use in expressions in a Part Studio, and assign a value. Use the variable in dimensions and expressions. Variables are features in Onshape, so the placement in the Feature list is important. Create a variable before the feature in which you will use it or create it on the fly during an operation that needs the value.

topics.title: Query Variable
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Query Variable
topics.desc: Create a selection group for use in expressions in a Part Studio. Use query the variable in dimensions and expressions. Query variables are features in Onshape, so the placement in the Feature list is important. Create a query variable before the feature in which you will use it or create it on the fly during an operation that needs the value.

topics.title: Composite Part
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Composite Part
topics.desc: A part comprised of selected bodies (parts, surfaces, curves, and/or points) grouped together to act as one part. You can create a closed composite part (one which consumes the bodies involved) or an open composite part (one that does not consume the bodies involved).

topics.title: Tag
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Tag
topics.desc: Tag sketch profile entities for use in Frames, parts to add or remove from Sheet metal forms, PCB holes for metadata used in PCB Studio board exports and imports, and parts to include in a custom standard content library. Select geometry, define orientation, and add properties.

topics.title: Frame
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Frame
topics.desc: Create a collection of swept bodies sharing a profile, arranged end-to-end.

topics.title: Onshape Frame Profiles Library
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Frame > Onshape Frame Profiles Library
topics.desc: The Onshape frame profiles library content is created by Onshape, kept in documents within Onshape and maintained by Onshape. There is never any risk of this content disappearing or not working from one release to another. We have integrated time-saving process in this workflow to simplify the insertion of frame profiles.

topics.title: Frame Trim
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Frame Trim
topics.desc: Create a collection of swept bodies sharing a profile, arranged end-to-end.

topics.title: Gusset
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Gusset
topics.desc: Create a collection of swept bodies sharing a profile, arranged end-to-end.

topics.title: End cap
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > End cap
topics.desc: Create one or more end caps for frame segments.

topics.title: Cut List
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Cut List
topics.desc: Create a Frame, that is a collection of swept bodies sharing a profile, arranged end-to-end.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Model
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Model
topics.desc: Create sheet metal parts by converting existing parts, extruding sketch curves (including arcs and splines to create rolled sheet metal), or thickening faces or sketches.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Flange
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Flange
topics.desc: Create a wall for each edge selected for a sheet metal model, connected by a bend.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Hem
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Hem
topics.desc: Create one or more hems on existing sheet metal parts.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Tab
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Tab
topics.desc: Add a tab to a sheet metal flange, remove interfering material if appropriate, or bridge two flanges from the same sheet metal model. Sheet metal tabs are reflected in the model and in the flat pattern.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Bend
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Bend
topics.desc: Bend a sheet metal model along a reference line, with additional bend control options.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Jog
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Jog
topics.desc: Bend a sheet metal model along a reference line, with additional bend control options.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Form
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Form
topics.desc: Create form features on existing sheet metal models. Forms can be selected from the current document, other documents, or a predefined library of sheet metal forms.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Form Library
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Form > Onshape Sheet Metal Forms Library
topics.desc: The Onshape sheet metal forms library content is created by Onshape, kept in documents within Onshape and maintained by Onshape. There is never any risk of this content disappearing or not working from one release to another. We have integrated time-saving process in this workflow to simplify the insertion of forms.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Loft
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Loft
topics.desc: Create a sheet metal part that transitions between two profiles.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Make Joint
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Make Joint
topics.desc: Join or extend existing sheet metal walls into a bend or rip (that is displayed in the Bend/Rip table), creating associativity between the two edges. You have the ability to configure and further define the style of the bend or rip once it is created. To modify an existing joint, use Modify joint.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Corner
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Corner
topics.desc: Modify a corner on a sheet metal model by selecting an edge, vertex, or face of the existing corner.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Bend Relief
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Bend Relief
topics.desc: Modify a bend relief (the small cut made where the bend end meets a free edge), and by specifying a shape, and either a depth and relief width scale, or specific bend relief depth. You are also able to select to extend the bend relief in the opposite direction in the case of a flange, for example.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Modify Joint
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Modify Joint
topics.desc: Editing an existing sheet metal model’s bends, rips, and joints using the Sheet metal table creates a Modify joint feature in the Feature list. Edit this feature as you would any other; right-click the feature entry to access the context menu.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Corner Break
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Corner Break
topics.desc: Break the corner on existing sheet metal parts by applying a fillet or chamfer. Select a corner edge or vertex and specify corner break type and distance. It is recommended to use this feature after all flanges and joints of the Sheet metal model are finalized.

topics.title: Sheet Metal Table and Flat View
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Table and Flat View
headings: Sheet Metal Table and Flat View
topics.desc: Edit an existing sheet metal model’s bends, rips, and joints. View the sheet metal flat pattern.

topics.title: Finish Sheet Metal Model
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Finish Sheet Metal Model
topics.desc: This tool deactivates one or more selected sheet metal models and causes them to be treated like any non-sheet metal solid parts. This allows you to perform post-fabrication operations on them, such as drilling at an angle through a face, welding corners, and adding form features and custom FeatureScript features.

topics.title: Flex PCB Model
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Flex PCB Model
topics.desc: Create flexible PCB parts by converting existing parts, extruding sketches, or thickening faces or sketches. Operations on PCB models are automatically represented as a flat pattern, and joints and bends are listed in a table.

topics.title: Finish Flex PCB Model
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Finish Flex PCB Model
topics.desc: Deactivates the selected flex PCB model and causes it to be treated like any non-flex PCB part. This allows the user to optionally perform post-finishing operations, and continue editing the part with non-PCB features.

topics.title: Add Custom Features
topics.path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Add Custom Features
headings: Open the document of a linked custom feature
topics.desc: Custom features (and custom tables) are written in a programming language called FeatureScript and are created in an Onshape tab called a Feature Studio. These custom features are able to be added to your Feature toolbar for use in documents to which you have write access. Custom tables are available immediately in the document in which they are created, and you can add them to any other document (from a version).

topics.title: Assemblies
topics.path: Assemblies
topics.desc: An Onshape Assembly tab is where you define a hierarchical structure of part and subassembly instances of an Assembly. It is also where you define degrees of freedom and relations. You are able to have more than one Assembly tab in a document. One Assembly can instance another Assembly as a subassembly, and/or instance a part directly. You are able to instance parts from the same document or other documents to which you have permissions (and that are versioned).

topics.title: Insert Parts and Assemblies
topics.path: Assemblies > Insert Parts and Assemblies
topics.desc: Insert Parts and Assemblies inserts instances of parts, assemblies, sketches and surfaces into the active Assembly. You can instance specific parts (released or unreleased), sketches and surfaces defined in a Part Studio (or the entire Part Studio), and assemblies defined in a different Assembly tab, as well as all of these things from other documents (linking documents).

topics.title: Linking Documents
topics.path: Assemblies > Insert Parts and Assemblies > Linking Documents
topics.desc: You can insert a part or assembly from a version of one Onshape document into an assembly in another Onshape Document, thereby linking the documents. Moving a part from one document to another creates a link to that part in any Assembly in which the part is previously inserted. You can also insert a part or assembly from a different version of the same document.

topics.title: Updating References
topics.path: Assemblies > Updating References
topics.desc: Onshape allows you to insert parts and assemblies from any document into any other document. We refer to this as linking documents since referencing a part or assembly that resides in one document from another document (or within different versions of the same document) creates a sort of virtual link between the two documents (or two versions of the same document).

topics.title: Instances List
topics.path: Assemblies > Instances List
topics.desc: The Insatances list in an Assembly tab contains a list of all part Instances, Groups, Mate connectors, Mates, and Relations defined for the Assembly. Use the context menu to act on any of these entities.

topics.title: Standard Content
topics.path: Assemblies > Standard Content
topics.desc: Onshape standard content is content created by Onshape, kept in a database in Onshape, and maintained by Onshape. Users can insert Standard content in their Assemblies. There is never any risk of this content disappearing or not working from one release to another. We have integrated time-saving process in this workflow to simplify the insertion of standard content.

topics.title: Onshape Standard Content Library
topics.path: Assemblies > Standard Content > Onshape Standard Content Library
topics.desc: This lists all of the standard content Onshape provides for your convenience. If the standard content you require is listed here, you don't have to model it - you can simply use the Insert parts and assemblies dialog to select the standard content you need. Check back here often to see what is available, since Onshape updates this list often.

topics.title: Custom Standard Content Libraries
topics.path: Assemblies > Standard Content > Custom Standard Content Libraries
topics.desc: Create your own Standard Content library for users to insert in their assemblies.

topics.title: Bill of Materials
topics.path: Assemblies > Bill of Materials (BOM)
topics.desc: Use the Onshape Bill of Materials (BOM) functionality to automatically create a BOM from any workspace Assembly. You can insert parts and assemblies into an Assembly post-release, from an Onshape version, or assemble the parts and sub-assemblies and then release the Assembly all at once. For more information on Release management, see Release Management.

topics.title: Working with the BOM Table
topics.path: Assemblies > Bill of Materials (BOM) > Working with the BOM Table
topics.desc: Perform several functions from the BOM table, such as inserting non-geometric items, generating next or missing part numbers, switching to a Part Studio or Assembly from an item, open a linked document, suppress/show parts or subassemblies, and export the table to a CSV file.

topics.title: BOM Table formatting
topics.path: Assemblies > Bill of Materials (BOM) > BOM Table Formatting
topics.desc: Add, remove, move, and resize columns, and sort items in the BOM table.

topics.title: BOM Table Templates
topics.path: Assemblies > Bill of Materials (BOM) > BOM Table Templates
topics.desc: Once you have edited the BOM format, you can save that as a template and use it.

topics.title: Mate Connector
topics.path: Assemblies > Mate Connector
headings: Flip primary axis of Mate connectors
Reorient secondary axis of Mate connectors
topics.desc: Mate connectors are local coordinate system entities located on or between entities and used within a Mate to locate and orient instances with respect to each other.

topics.title: Mates
topics.path: Assemblies > Mates
topics.desc: Mates in Onshape are different than mates in old CAD systems. There is only one Onshape Mate between any two instances, and the movement (degrees of freedom) between those two instances is embedded in the Mate. Mates contain their own coordinate systems, so you ever only need to use one Mate to define the degrees of freedom between two entities.

topics.title: Fastened Mate
topics.path: Assemblies > Mates > Fastened Mate
topics.desc: Mate two entities and remove all degrees of freedom between them.

topics.title: Revolute Mate
topics.path: Assemblies > Mates > Revolute Mate
topics.desc: Mate two entities allowing rotational movement about the Z axis. (Rz).

topics.title: Slider Mate
topics.path: Assemblies > Mates > Slider Mate
topics.desc: Mate two entities allowing translational movement along the Z axis. (Tz).

topics.title: Planar Mate
topics.path: Assemblies > Mates > Planar Mate
topics.desc: Mate two entities allowing translational movement along the X axis and the Y axis, and rotational movement about the Z axis (Ty, Tx, Rz).

topics.title: Cylindrical Mate
topics.path: Assemblies > Mates > Cylindrical Mate
topics.desc: Mate two entities allowing translational movement along the Z axis and rotational movement about the Z axis (Tz, Rz).

topics.title: Pin Slot Mate
topics.path: Assemblies > Mates > Pin Slot Mate
topics.desc: Mate two entities allowing rotational movement about the Z axis and translational movement along the X axis. (Rz, Tx).

topics.title: Ball Mate
topics.path: Assemblies > Mates > Ball Mate
topics.desc: Mate two entities allowing rotational movement about the X, Y and Z axis (Rx, Ry, Rz).

topics.title: Parallel Mate
topics.path: Assemblies > Mates > Parallel Mate
topics.desc: Mate two entities allowing individual translational movement along any axis, and parallel rotation along any axis.

topics.title: Tangent Mate
topics.path: Assemblies > Mates > Tangent Mate
topics.desc: Mate two entities tangent to the selected faces, edges, or vertices.

topics.title: Width Mate
topics.path: Assemblies > Mates > Width Mate
headings: Keeping 1 part symmetrical between 2 Width mate connectors.
Keeping 2 parts symmetrical between 2 Width mate connectors
Using 2 Width mate connections to center entities in a u-joint
Centering a Jackhammer handle shaft between its end caps
Width mate used with an asymmetric part
topics.desc: Mate up to two tabs to constrain them symmetrically between two mate connectors. Allow translation and normal rotation on a slot's center plane. The first selection defines the item to be centered. The second selection defines the center plane.

topics.title: Group
topics.path: Assemblies > Group
topics.desc: Use Group to fix the position of selected instances relative to one another within the assembly. It is very convenient when the instances were all modeled in the same Part Studio in the correct locations relative to one another. Group enables you to keep that relative positioning without having to create Mates.

topics.title: Snap Mode
topics.path: Assemblies > Snap Mode
topics.desc: Automatically create a Mate when inserting an entity into an Assembly, using explicitly created Mate connectors on the entity being inserted. Also, drag one entity (by a Mate connector) to snap to a Mate connector on another entity. Both methods result in an open Mate dialog so you are able to fine tune the Mate type and alignment.

topics.title: Show Mates
topics.path: Assemblies > Show Mates Mode
topics.desc: In this mode, you are able to hover over or select instances in the graphics area or Instances list to show the mates for that instance.

topics.title: Replicate
topics.path: Assemblies > Replicate
topics.desc: Replicate takes a seed entity or entities as input, a bolt for instance, and locates geometry identical to that which the seed is mated to (based on an additional selection). The seed is then replicated and mated to that matching geometry.

topics.title: Replace Instance
topics.path: Assemblies > Replace Instance
topics.desc: Replace instance allows you to replace selected or all instances of a part, surface, sketch, or subassembly within an assembly. Even if the replacement component is slightly different (for example, a derivative of the part), it will be inserted and all previously associated mates reapplied.

topics.title: Assembly Linear Pattern
topics.path: Assemblies > Assembly Linear Pattern
topics.desc: Pattern selected entities and arrange them in a row pattern. For information on creating circular patterns, see Assembly Circular Pattern.

topics.title: Assembly Circular Pattern
topics.path: Assemblies > Assembly Circular Pattern
topics.desc: Pattern selected entities about an axis. For information on creating linear patterns, see Assembly Linear Pattern.

topics.title: Assembly Mirror
topics.path: Assemblies > Assembly Mirror
headings: Symmetric mirror of a part or surface (via Transform)
topics.desc: Create mirrored instances of a part, surface, or subassembly. Specify the mirror plane and select a mirror strategy.

topics.title: Relations
topics.path: Assemblies > Relations
topics.desc: Use relations on mates to constrain degrees of freedom between mates.

topics.title: Gear Relation
topics.path: Assemblies > Relations > Gear Relation
topics.desc: Relate two Mates with revolute degrees of freedom. The relation creates a constant ratio of angular rotation between the Mates. If either mated part is moved, the other will move rotationally.

topics.title: Rack and Pinion Relation
topics.path: Assemblies > Relations > Rack and Pinion Relation
topics.desc: Relate a Mate with a rotational degree of freedom to a Mate with a linear degree of freedom.

topics.title: Screw Relation
topics.path: Assemblies > Relations > Screw Relation
topics.desc: Constrain the rotational degree of freedom in one Cylindrical Mate to the translational degree of freedom in the same Cylindrical Mate.

topics.title: Linear Relation
topics.path: Assemblies > Relations > Linear Relation
topics.desc: Constrain the linear motion between two Mates to change at a constant ratio. The first Mate will move linearly in one direction as the other Mate is moved linearly in one direction.

topics.title: Named Positions
topics.path: Assemblies > Named Positions
topics.desc: Assign a name to a specific position (that is, the Mate degree of freedom values, and absolute transforms for instances with no Mates) of the assembly and switch to a particular named position easily at any time. Keep in mind that the Mate values are relative and are able to be satisfied even if both sides of the Mate have moved.

topics.title: Display States
topics.path: Assemblies > Display States
topics.desc: Assign a name to a specific display state (that is, with certain parts, subassemblies, or mates hidden or in view) of the assembly and switch to a particular display state easily at any time.

topics.title: Create Part Studio in Context
topics.path: Assemblies > Create Part Studio in Context
topics.desc: Create a new Part Studio in the context of an existing assembly; positioning the assembly specifically for use when modeling the part. The assembly appears in the Part Studio as context graphics to be used for reference.

topics.title: Simulation
topics.path: Assemblies > Simulation
headings: Load direction arrow and context menu
topics.desc: Simulation, available to Enterprise and Professional plan subscribers, is used to evaluate the stresses and displacements between externally-loaded instances in an Assembly, allowing you to examine how an assembly reflects the loads, materials, and boundary conditions found in real-world use.

topics.title: Modal Simulation
topics.path: Assemblies > Simulation > Modal Simulation
topics.desc: Modal analysis, or more specifically, natural frequency analysis is used to provide information on the stiffness or mechanical resonance of an assembly structure. It is used by designers and engineers who require vibrational analysis within Onshape and is commonly used in industrial equipment, automotive, and aerospace industries, among others. Modal analysis is often required for subsequent dynamic analysis; for example, modal frequency response and modal transient analysis are used in safety calculations.

topics.title: Asynchronous Simulation
topics.path: Assemblies > Simulation > Asynchronous Simulation
topics.desc: With Asynchronous Simulation, a user runs simulations independent of their active modeling session. Simulation results are permanently stored in a Results and history table in the Simulation panel. Simulation results display the status of all jobs in the queue, in progress, and completed.

topics.title: Rigid Body
topics.path: Assemblies > Simulation > Rigid Body
topics.desc: Select bodies to be included in the Simulation while remaining non-deformable.

topics.title: Exploded Views
topics.path: Assemblies > Exploded Views
topics.desc: Manually manipulate an assembly into an exploded view using the manipulator to drag components or groups of components from their current positions to a new position. The steps are recorded in the Exploded views panel, complete with the ability to reorder and otherwise edit the view.

topics.title: Assembly Variable Table
topics.path: Assemblies > Assembly Variable Table
topics.desc: A Variable table allows you to create, view, and edit variable information in the current Part Studio or Assembly. The Variable table is located on the right side of the graphics area with the BOM table, Configuration panel, Exploded views, and Named positions. A Variable table is created in a document and the variables therein are immediately available for use in all Part Studios and Assemblies in that document workspace.

topics.title: Drawings
topics.path: Drawings
topics.desc: You have the ability to create mechanical drawings from within Onshape Part Studios and Assemblies and also of entire Part Studios. All Onshape drawings are based on the .DWG file format (drawing database) and the .DXF file format (Drawing Interchange File) is also supported.

topics.title: Drawing Basics
topics.path: Drawings > Drawing Basics
topics.desc: This section covers the basics of working with Drawings, including creating drawings, basic drawing workflow, and navigating within drawings.

topics.title: Creating a Drawing
topics.path: Drawings > Drawing Basics > Creating a Drawing
topics.desc: When you create a drawing of a part, curve, or surface in a Part Studio, or in an Assembly, the drawing contains default views. You are also able to create an empty drawing using the menu in the lower left corner of the window and select Create Drawing.

topics.title: Custom Templates
topics.path: Drawings > Drawing Basics > Custom Templates
topics.desc: Drawing templates are comprised of a drawing format that includes the title block, border, zones, properties and styles. Once defined, the drawing template is available for reuse when new Drawings are created. In addition to allowing the creation of custom templates from scratch, Onshape also provides a number of public drawing templates to use and customize.

topics.title: Sheets
topics.path: Drawings > Sheets
topics.desc: An Onshape sheet is a page of a drawing which represents a single sheet of paper in a printed version of a drawing. View the sheets of a drawing and their contents with the Sheet flyout, located on the left side of the interface.

topics.title: Styles
topics.path: Drawings > Styles
topics.desc: Drawing styles are a collection of visual settings you can apply to one or more dimensions, without having them affect all dimensions globally, as when they are edited in the Properties panel. Styles are located in a panel on the right side of the drawings area. Click the icon to open the panel, and click again to close the panel.

topics.title: Drawing Properties
topics.path: Drawings > Properties
shortcuts: Right-click on an empty area in the drawing and select Drawing properties
headings: To select a DWT from the current document
To select a DWT from other documents
topics.desc: Click the icon on the right side of the drawings area to open the Drawing properties panel. Use these settings to define the defaults for your drawing. Individual drawing entities may be changed separately, but these settings apply to all entities in a drawing as a default. Once you have your drawing properties set to your satisfaction, you can save the drawing and its settings as a template.

topics.title: Drawing Properties - Units and Precision
topics.path: Drawings > Properties > Units and Precision
topics.desc: Edit the current drawing's Primary and Dual units, and Leading and trailing zeros. Change each option by clicking the drop down menu arrows on the right side of the menu and selecting an option.

topics.title: Drawing Properties - Dimensions
topics.path: Drawings > Properties > Dimensions
topics.desc: Edit the current drawing's font, text height, color, text alignment, text gaps, geometry gaps, and more. Change each option by clicking the drop down menu arrows on the right side of the menu and selecting an option.

topics.title: Drawing Properties - Annotations
topics.path: Drawings > Properties > Annotations
topics.desc: Edit the current drawing's font, text height, arrowhead length and type, and color of each annotation type in your drawing. Supply defaults for all annotations at once, or Notes, Callouts, Datums, Geometric tolerances, Surface finish symbols, Weld symbols, Hole callouts, and Bend notes (for sheet metal) separately.

topics.title: Drawing Properties - Views
topics.path: Drawings > Properties > Views
topics.desc: Edit the current drawing's projection angle, the color and thickness of your drawing's visible edges, tangent edges, hidden edges, cutting lines, arrowheads, view labels and more.

topics.title: Drawing Properties - Construction Geometry
topics.path: Drawings > Properties > Construction Geometry
topics.desc: Edit the color and thickness of the drawing's centerlines and centermarks, as well as the style, color, and thickness of the drawing's virtual sharps. Use the Part Studio sketches section to edit the format of sketches brought into the drawing.

topics.title: Drawing Properties - Formats
topics.path: Drawings > Properties > Formats
topics.desc: These properties enable / disable selection of objects in a drawing's border frame, border zone, and title block. The default for a new drawing is Locked; you are not able to immediately select objects in the title block, border, or border zones.

topics.title: Drawing Properties - Tables
topics.path: Drawings > Properties > Tables
topics.desc: Edit Bill of Material (BOM), custom, cut list, hole, revision, and other tables created in the current drawing.

topics.title: Drawing Properties - Inspection
topics.path: Drawings > Properties > Inspection
topics.desc: Edit the appearance of inspection items in the current drawing.

topics.title: MBD Status
topics.path: Drawings > MBD Status
topics.desc: The MBD status panel lists the inserted part's model-based definitions data (annotations and dimensions) not visible in the drawing. If any visible data is deleted from a drawing view, it is also displayed in this panel and can be shown again.

topics.title: Views
topics.path: Drawings > Views
headings: Moving a view to another sheet
Moving a linked view to another sheet
topics.desc: When you create a drawing from a part, curve, surface, or subassembly, you have the ability to create it without any views, by default, or with 4 standard views: top, front, right, and isometric. Typically, the projection of the views depends on the standard chosen: first angle projection for ISO standard and third angle projection for ANSI standard, you can also use a custom template and select the projection, or change the projection after the drawing is created.

topics.title: Projected View
topics.path: Drawings > Views > Projected View
topics.desc: Create a new view by projecting (folding) out an existing view.

topics.title: Auxiliary View
topics.path: Drawings > Views > Auxiliary View
topics.desc: Create an auxiliary view; an orthographic view that is folded out 90 degrees from a selected edge in the parent view (usually from a slanted edge). Alternatively, you can create a sketch line or centerline about which to orient the auxiliary view.

topics.title: Drawing Section View
topics.path: Drawings > Views > Section View
topics.desc: Create a section view, jogged section view, or partial section view of an existing view (including a section view) by placing a cutting plane line (or lines) and specifying a direction and label.

topics.title: Aligned Section View
topics.path: Drawings > Views > Aligned Section View
topics.desc: Create a section view in which some portions of the view have been cut on a plane not parallel to the view plane and those portions have been rotated onto the view plane. This view type is most commonly used on cylindrical parts with some symmetry but not fully symmetrical.

topics.title: Broken-Out Section View
topics.path: Drawings > Views > Broken-Out Section View
topics.desc: Create a broken-out section view to cut away a portion of the model in a drawing view by defining a closed profile with the Spline tool.

topics.title: Detail View
topics.path: Drawings > Views > Detail View
topics.desc: Use Detail view to select an area of an existing view to enlarge for more detail.

topics.title: Break View
topics.path: Drawings > Views > Break View
topics.desc: Use Break view to shorten an existing view by trimming out a portion.

topics.title: Crop View
topics.path: Drawings > Views > Crop View
topics.desc: To crop a view, sketch a circle, spline, or polygon around the area you wish to keep.

topics.title: Drawing Flat Pattern View
topics.path: Drawings > Views > Flat Pattern View
topics.desc: A sheet metal flat pattern view can only be inserted from the Insert dialog. Once inserted from this dialog it can be placed into the sheet.

topics.title: View Context Menu
topics.path: Drawings > Views > View Context Menu
topics.desc: Hover over any view and right-click the mouse to open a context menu on any view to access a list of command options for that view. These command options are listed below. Not all options listed here are available for every type of view.

topics.title: Drawing Dimensions
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions
topics.desc: Place a dimension on any type of curve in a drawing.

topics.title: Drawing - Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > Dimension
topics.desc: Known as the smart dimension tool, this places several types of dimensions on a curve in a drawing. The type of curve selected determines the type of dimension that is placed.

topics.title: Drawing - Chamfer Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > Chamfer Dimension
topics.desc: Place a note or dimension on a chamfered edge.

topics.title: Drawing - Maximum or Minimum Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > Maximum or Minimum Dimension
topics.desc: Place a minimum or maximum dimension directly to any combination of arcs, circles and any other geometry type, excluding curves.

topics.title: Drawing - 2 Point Linear Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > 2 Point Linear Dimension
topics.desc: Measure the distance between two points. Create horizontal, vertical, and rotated linear dimensions.

topics.title: Drawing - Point to Line Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > Point to Line Dimension
topics.desc: Measure the distance between a point and a line. Create horizontal, vertical, and rotated linear dimensions.

topics.title: Drawing - Line to Line Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > Line to Line Dimension
topics.desc: Create dimensions between parallel lines.

topics.title: Drawing - Line to Line Angular Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > Line to Line Angular Dimension
headings: Drawing - Line to Line Angular Dimension
topics.desc: Measure the interior angle between the two legs and the exterior angle formed by two lines.

topics.title: Drawing - 3 Point Angular Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > 3 Point Angular Dimension
topics.desc: Measure an angle by selecting 3 points, including a vertex and two points on the legs.

topics.title: Drawing - Arc Length Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > Arc Length Dimension
topics.desc: Measure the length of an arc.

topics.title: Drawing - Radial Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > Radial Dimension
topics.desc: Measure the radial dimension of a circle, arc, or circular arc centermark.

topics.title: Drawing - Diameter Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > Diameter Dimension
topics.desc: Measure the diameter of a circle, arc or circular arc centermark, including silhouette edges.

topics.title: Drawing - Foreshorten Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > Foreshorten Dimension
headings: Converting between a foreshortened and direct dimension
topics.desc: Place a foreshorten dimension on a silhouette edge, or on a centerline and an arc or circle edge, to create a half-diameter dimension in a Drawing.

topics.title: Drawing - Ordinate Dimension
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > Ordinate Dimension
topics.desc: Create ordinate dimensions (X, Y pairs) for a feature measured from a datum. Ordinate dimensions created as a group move together when one is moved.

topics.title: Drawing - Hole/Thread Callout
topics.path: Drawings > Dimensions > Hole/Thread Callout
topics.desc: Apply a hole callout to a hole or thread, automatically inserting the metadata of the hole or thread.

topics.title: Datum
topics.path: Drawings > Datum
topics.desc: Use Datum to create and place associative datum symbols to the drawing view on a surface that appears as a linear or circular edge to identify datum planes in the part.

topics.title: Geometric Tolerances
topics.path: Drawings > Geometric Tolerance
topics.desc: Often associated with datum, use Geometric tolerance to create and place basic dimension notations in the drawing.

topics.title: Surface Finish
topics.path: Drawings > Surface Finish
topics.desc: Place a surface finish symbol on the edge of a circular view or away from edges.

topics.title: Weld Symbol
topics.path: Drawings > Weld Symbol
topics.desc: Place weld symbols on a drawing. Weld standards default to the standard specified for the drawing. To change the weld standard, access the drawing’s Properties flyout located on the right side of the page.

topics.title: Edge Condition Symbol
topics.path: Drawings > Edge Condition Symbol
topics.desc: Place an edge condition symbol on a Drawing to show the acceptable state of an edge or corner created during machining.

topics.title: Note
topics.path: Drawings > Note
topics.desc: Add single or multi-line text notes to any drawing, wherever you want, and use them to fill in the title blocks as well. You have the ability to define the size of the text box as well as format the text itself and optionally include a leader or many leaders. You also have the ability to rotate the orientation of the note and create additional leaders.

topics.title: Callout (Balloon)
topics.path: Drawings > Callout (Balloon)
headings: To group a callout during creation:
To group a callout to a view:
topics.desc: Create and edit callouts (balloons) with a leader line. Callouts are associative with the part metadata of the document and a BOM table when a BOM App is used within your Onshape document. When a BOM table is present, the callout defaults to use the Item Number in the table. If the table order is changed, use the Update Drawing feature to update the callouts.

topics.title: Table
topics.path: Drawings > Table
topics.desc: Add fully-customizable tables to any drawing.

topics.title: BOM Table
topics.path: Drawings > BOM Table
topics.desc: Insert a Bill of Materials table from an Onshape BOM table, uploaded file, or an authorized app. You are also able to use the Balloon tool to automatically pull identifiers from the BOM to label the drawing. See Balloon for more information.

topics.title: Cut List Table
topics.path: Drawings > Cut List Table
topics.desc: Insert a Bill of Materials table from an Onshape BOM table, uploaded file, or an authorized app. You are also able to use the Balloon tool to automatically pull identifiers from the BOM to label the drawing. See Balloon for more information.

topics.title: Hole Table
topics.path: Drawings > Hole Table
topics.desc: Insert a hole table for a view or multiple views of a common, singular part (and not an entire Part Studio). Style the table as you would any other table, and hover over a table row for cross-highlighting in the drawing.

topics.title: Custom Table
topics.path: Drawings > Custom Table
topics.desc: Insert a custom table into a drawing. Custom tables tabulate Part Studio data. Updates to the Part Studio update the data in the custom table. See Updating a Drawing for more information.

topics.title: Revision Table
topics.path: Drawings > Revision Table
headings: Editing column headers and title of table
topics.desc: Insert a revision table to record the revisions of the drawing created during the release management process. Style the table as you would any other table and adjust properties of the table through the Properties panel. As the drawing moves through the release management process, further revisions and table information are updated automatically.

topics.title: Drawing Construction Tools
topics.path: Drawings > Drawing Construction Tools
topics.desc: Onshape provides tools for creating sheet geometry: drawing entities like lines and centerlines, created on the sheet outside of a view and meant to represent some part of the 3D model.

topics.title: Drawing Sketch Tools
topics.path: Drawings > Drawing Sketch Tools
headings: Drawing views in which hatch regions can be applied/edited
topics.desc: Onshape provides tools for creating sheet sketch geometry: drawing entities like lines, circles, and rectangles, created on the sheet.

topics.title: Working with Drawing Constraints
topics.path: Drawings > Working with Drawing Constraints
topics.desc: Apply constraints between sketch entities and drawing view geometry.

topics.title: Insert DXF or DWG
topics.path: Drawings > Insert DXF or DWG
topics.desc: Insert the contents of a DXF or DWG file as Onshape drawing entities. Use this tool as a method to create a custom template; for more information see Custom Drawing Templates.

topics.title: Insert Image
topics.path: Drawings > Insert Image
topics.desc: You can insert and scale JPG, PNG, and GIF images on a drawing sheet, such as a logo and QR and bar codes.

topics.title: Format Painter
topics.path: Drawings > Format Painter
topics.desc: Use the Styles panel format of one dimension or annotation to format additional dimensions or annotations in the drawing.

topics.title: Inspection Item
topics.path: Drawings > Inspection Item
topics.desc: Add Inspection items to the drawing, on multiple sheets, numbered, and attached to the desired annotation or callout type, including: dimensions, tolerances (including for separate frames), surface symbols, notes, etc. Note that Inspection items cannot be attached to datums.

topics.title: Updating a Drawing
topics.path: Drawings > Updating a Drawing
topics.desc: When an underlying Part Studio or Assembly of a drawing is changed, the drawing may need to be updated, as indicated by the active yellow icon (the inactive icon is grayed out). Changes that trigger this condition may be seemingly insignificant, like moving a sketch dimension or hiding a construction plane in a Part Studio. To understand better why this button is active, check the History of the document to view recent changes.

topics.title: Dangling entities
topics.path: Drawings > Updating a Drawing > Dangling Entities
topics.desc: A dangling entity in a drawing is an entity that has lost one (or more) of its reference points. Dimensions, section lines, note leaders, callouts, centermarks, and geometric tolerances are all examples of entities that could become dangling (broken) after a drawing update. This is to be expected, especially if the change to the part or assembly was significant.

topics.title: Importing a Drawing
topics.path: Drawings > Importing a Drawing
topics.desc: This section covers how to import Drawings. They can be imported from the Documents page where they automatically become a new document, or within a document, where they automatically become a tab inside that document.

topics.title: Exporting a Drawing
topics.path: Drawings > Exporting a Drawing
topics.desc: You can export Onshape drawings to the following file types: PDF, DWG, DXF, DWT, SVG, PNG, JPEG, and CSV (for Drawing Inspection item lists). To set up Export rules for drawings, including exporting the inspection symbol count of a drawing, see how to set the preference in your account under Managing Your Onshape Plan.

topics.title: Printing a Drawing
topics.path: Drawings > Printing a Drawing
topics.desc: This topic covers how to print Drawings.

topics.title: Variable Studios
topics.path: Variable Studios
topics.desc: This topic explains the functionality and mechanics of using a Variable Studio to create variables that can be used in the document in which they are created as well in other documents.

topics.title: Feature Studios
topics.path: Feature Studios
topics.desc: A Feature Studio is a tab containing FeatureScript, a programming language used to define your own custom features in Onshape.

topics.title: Render Studios
topics.path: Render Studios
topics.desc: This Onshape Render Studio application, free for Enterprise and Professional plan subscribers, allows you to create photorealistic scenes from your imported Part Studios or Assemblies. Use scenes to test model appearances and materials, lighting and camera setups, and environments. Export scenes as .jpg- or .png-formatted images to market your rendered designs.

topics.title: Render Studio Basics
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Basics
topics.desc: This section explains Render Studio basic navigation and workflow.

topics.title: Render Studio Interface
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface
topics.desc: The sections below explain how each area of the Render Studio tab's interface works. You can create multiple Render Studio tabs, each containing a dashboard with a number of Render Studio scenes.

topics.title: Render Studio Interface - Toolbar
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Toolbar
topics.desc: Located at the top of the page, the toolbar contains several commands that are commonly performed when working in Render Studio.

topics.title: Render Studio Interface - Scene List
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Scene List
topics.desc: Located on the left side of the page, the Scene list provides part, Part Studio and Assembly information for the current Render Studio scene.

topics.title: Render Studio Interface - Graphics Area
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Graphics Area
topics.desc: The Graphics area is where the scene is visually located. It appears in the center of the Render Studio application.

topics.title: Render Studio Interface - Appearances Library
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Appearances Library
topics.desc: Located at the bottom of the page, the Appearances library contains all the standard attribute combinations that are applied to parts, part faces, or surfaces, to provide a material texture, as well as functions that are applied to appearance parameters.

topics.title: Appearance Functions
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Appearances Library > Appearance Functions
topics.desc: Functions are a special type of appearance that perform a specific action on a part's appearance parameter. When a scene is created, every part has a default set of appearance parameters, viewable in the Appearance panel on the right.

topics.title: Appearance Modifiers
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Appearances Library > Appearance Modifiers
topics.desc: Modifiers are a special type of appearance that are used to modify other appearances. These modifiers do not overwrite the prior appearance. Instead, the modifier is associated to the Base material parameter of the new modifier appearance.

topics.title: Textures and Bump Maps
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Appearances Library > Textures and Bump Maps
topics.desc: Apply textures, custom image textures, bump textures, and custom bump textures to a part's appearance parameters in Render Studio.

topics.title: Light Emission
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Appearances Library > Light Emission
topics.desc: There are several appearances devoted to adding and emitting light from a part, surface, or face in a scene. Which light appearance is used depends on the light source and how the scene in question should be lighted.

topics.title: Render Studio Interface - Environments Library
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Environments Library
topics.desc: Located at the bottom of the page, the Environments library contains all the standard environments that are added as the backdrop for the Part Studio, Assembly, and parts in the scene. An environment also provides scene illumination.

topics.title: Render Studio Interface - Appearance Panel
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Appearance Panel
topics.desc: Located at the right of the page, the Appearance panel displays an editable list of parameters for the appearance of the selected object. The Appearance is material-specific (for example, Fabric, Glass, or Masonry), and the available panel parameters change, depending on the selected Appearance.

topics.title: Render Studio Interface - Environment Panel
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Environment Panel
topics.desc: Located at the right of the page, the Environment panel displays an editable list of parameters for the scene environment. The available panel parameters change, depending on the selected Environment. Click the Environment panel icon to open the panel.

topics.title: Render Studio Interface - Camera Panel
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Camera Panel
topics.desc: Located at the right of the page, the Camera panel displays an editable list of parameters for the Camera directed at the selected object, such as Field of view, Focal length, Position, Rotation, Background, Depth of Field, Exposure, Tone and contrast, Vignetting, and other Advanced options.

topics.title: Render Studio Interface - Scene Panel
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Scene Panel
topics.desc: Located at the right of the page, the Scene panel displays an editable list of global parameters for the Scene list. Click the Scene panel icon to open the panel.

topics.title: Render Studio Interface - Render Options
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Render Options
topics.desc: Render options determine how the scene is output to a JPEG or PNG image file. Once scene edits are completed, click the Render scene button on the toolbar to open the Render options dialog.

topics.title: Render Studio Advanced
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Advanced
topics.desc: Render Studio Advanced provides additional functionality when working in Render Studio tabs.

topics.title: AxF Appearance (Render Studio Advanced)
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Advanced > AxF Appearance
topics.desc: X-rite AxF appearances are a self-contained file format which are output by X-rite scanning devices such as the TAC-7, MA-T12 and MetaVue VS3200. Unlike a texture file these files completely describe an appearances properties and may include both uniform and spatially varying information.

topics.title: Appearance Set (Render Studio Advanced)
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Advanced > Appearance Set
topics.desc: The Appearance set is an Appearance modifier that is assigned to an entity (Part Studio, Assembly, part, face). Once assigned, multiple appearances can be added to the set in the Appearance panel. Switching between appearances in the set provides a quick and easy method to experiment with appearance variations.

topics.title: Volume (Render Studio Advanced)
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Advanced > Volume
topics.desc: A volume is a cubic region in which the volumetric portion of an appearance exists and is rendered. The volume can optionally be an OpenVDB 3D texture. Non-advanced users can open a scene that contains Volumes, but their properties are non-editable.

topics.title: Light (Render Studio Advanced)
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Advanced > Light
topics.desc: A Light is a Render Studio Advanced scene entity that creates an explicit source of luminescence, with position and direction. Light is emitted into the scene based on one of 3 distribution types (Diffuse, Spot, and Profile) that determines how light varies with the angle to the light source. Lights may also have a surface area that cause them to cast softer shadows.

topics.title: Render Studio Examples and Resources
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Examples and Resources
topics.desc: This topic includes additional examples and resources to get the most out of the Render Studio application.

topics.title: Render Studio Libraries
topics.path: Render Studios > Render Studio Libraries
topics.desc: This topic provides tables that outline the standard Render Studio Appearances and Environments libraries and their descriptions.

topics.title: PCB Studio
topics.path: PCB Studios
headings: View cube and Camera and Render options
Importing a PTC Creo hint.map file
Translate the CAD data to ECAD
Export the data and download the file
topics.desc: This Onshape PCB Studios application, free for Enterprise and Professional plan subscribers, allows you to create models using ECAD files for reference. PCB Studios helps you create shapes for printed circuit boards using Onshape, export those models created in Onshape in an IDF format and send them to an electrical engineer to use to create PCB designs in an ECAD system.

topics.title: Altium 365 Integration
topics.path: PCB Studios > Altium 365 Integration
topics.desc: Altium 365 Integration links a user's Altium account to their Onshape account. Once integrated, the user can browse Altium workspaces, and import Altium boards directly into PCB Studio without the need to use files. When an Altium board is imported, it can be created in Onshape using the same tools already used for boards imported from file formats like IDF.

topics.title: Rigid-Flex PCB
topics.path: PCB Studios > Rigid-Flex PCB
topics.desc: Import Rigid-flex PCBs into Onshape from Altium 365 or an IDX file, or create Rigid-flex PCBs in Onshape that can be exported to an IDX file.

topics.title: CAM Studios
topics.path: CAM Studios
topics.desc: Onshape CAM Studios allow you to create cutting strategies, or toolpaths, based off of CAD model geometry. The strategies are posted into a language that a CNC machine interprets called Gcode. The CNC machine uses this code to manipulate the machine axes and cutting tools to remove material from a piece of stock as a form of subtractive manufacturing.

topics.title: Account Menu
topics.path: Account Menu
topics.desc: The Account menu, located under your name in the upper-right corner of the interface, allows you to access My account, Action items, View support tickets, Switch to. . . , Company or Enterprise settings, and Sign out.

topics.title: My Account Settings
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings
shortcuts: Shortcut toolbars - Customize the shortcut toolbars available for Sketch tools, Feature tools, Assembly tools, and Drawing tools.
topics.desc: My account settings is where you can manage and maintain your Onshape account, set preferences, notifications settings, security and all the account settings, as explained in this topic. See blow for more information.

topics.title: My Account - Profile
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Profile
topics.desc: The Onshape user profile displays general information about you and your account, such as Name, username, nickname, bio, and documentation name.

topics.title: My Account - Emails
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Emails
topics.desc: Displays email settings. Add, remove, or edit your primary or other emails.

topics.title: My Account - Preferences
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Preferences
topics.desc: Displays preference settings for your account, such as language, startup page, units, mouse controls, toolbars, keyboard shortcuts, and more.

topics.title: Export Rule Conventions
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Preferences > Export Rule Conventions
topics.desc: Some default Onshape properties, and all custom properties, can be used as export rule conventions.

topics.title: My Account - Notifications
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Notifications
topics.desc: Displays email and mobile notifications settings for shares and comments.

topics.title: My Account - Security
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Security
topics.desc: Displays security settings, where you can reset your password.

topics.title: My Account - Devices
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Devices
topics.desc: Displays devices settings, where you can create device profiles for use with Onshape.

topics.title: My Account - Applications
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Applications
topics.desc: Displays applications settings, where you can add or remove the applications you use with your Onshape account.

topics.title: My Account - Integrations
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Integrations
topics.desc: Displays the integrations settings, where you can grant Onshape access to your Dropbox, Google Drive, or Microsoft OneDrive account (separately).

topics.title: My Account - Developer
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Developer
topics.desc: Allow users to create api keys for managing apps.

topics.title: My Account - Early Visibility
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Early Visibility
topics.desc: Displays the early visibility settings, where you can manage access to the Onshape early visibility program, allowing you to test functionality that is under development.

topics.title: My Account - Subscription
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Subscriptions
topics.desc: Displays subscription settings, where you can view, edit, update, or cancel your subscription.

topics.title: My Account - Payment Options
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Payment Option
topics.desc: Displays payment option settings, where you can edit credit card and billing information.

topics.title: My Account - Payment History
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Payment History
topics.desc: Displays your payment history. Only Company account Owners and Administrators can see this information for Professional plans. Users in Standard and Free plans can see their history (in case a Free user has downgraded from another plan).

topics.title: My Account - Teams
topics.path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Teams
topics.desc: Displays team settings, where you can add or remove teams.

topics.title: Action Items
topics.path: Account Menu > Action Items
topics.desc: Action items are a sortable list of tasks that can be assigned by you or to you by another user within your Company/Enterprise. They can be release tasks or comments and can have the status of open or closed. Action items show up on the Enterprise tab bar at the top of the Onshape application.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings
topics.desc: View the account setting for your company (Company settings), Classroom (Classroom settings), or enterprise (Enterprise settings).

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Users
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Users
headings: Adding users via CSV file import
Adding users via the RMB context menu
Adding a guest user through Enterprise settings
Adding a guest user through the Share dialog
Adding a guest user through the Project dialog
topics.desc: Invite or add new users to your company/classroom/enterprise, view the list of current users, search for a particular user, delete selected users, and see whether a user is a Guest user. Only the company/classroom/enterprise Owner and the Admin (or Educator in the case of Classrooms) have the ability to add users to and remove users from the subscription.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Teams
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Teams
topics.desc: Create teams of users to group users together for the purpose of making sharing more efficient; once the team is created, you can select the team name instead of entering many users' individual email addresses during a Share operation. All team members must be users in the company/classroom/enterprise.

topics.title: Enterprise Settings - Aliases
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Aliases
topics.desc: Aliases are distribution lists for the Release management workflow. Only Administrators can create Aliases and assign other users or Teams to an alias. Specifically, an Administrator needs the Manage users and teams global permission in order to create aliases and assign other users or teams to an Alias.

topics.title: Enterprise Settings - Global Permissions
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Global Permissions
topics.desc: Global permissions control user access to Enterprise-level operations and information. Only the enterprise administrator or another user with administrator rights can grant Global permissions to users. The user who creates the Enterprise account becomes the first administrator of the account and is assigned the Enterprise administrator global permission.

topics.title: Enterprise settings - Connections
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Connections
topics.desc: Establish a connection to share data between an outside enterprise to one or more users in your enterprise. Data is not shared with your entire enterprise, only users you specify.

topics.title: Enterprise Settings - Authentication
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Authentication
topics.desc: Configure and manage two-factor authentication (2FA), single sign on (SSO), and domain verification.

topics.title: Enterprise Settings - Project Roles
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Project Roles
topics.desc: Project roles are used to group users into functional roles with associated permissions. For example, you may have Project roles like Designer, Engineer, Reviewer, and Vendor. These roles act as buckets that you will later group specific users into when you’re creating a Project.

topics.title: Enterprise Settings - Permission Schemes
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Permission Schemes
topics.desc: Project roles and Permission schemes work in tandem to apply access permission to documents grouped together within a Project. A Project references only one Permission scheme, which is comprised of Project roles specifying the permissions. Permission schemes are a named table of Role-Permission set pairs.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Properties/Custom Properties
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Properties/Custom Properties
topics.desc: Access the metadata definitions for Onshape objects (what drives the data displayed in object Properties dialogs and Bill of materials (BOM)), view these metadata definitions, and create new properties for use in Company/Classroom/Enterprise-owned documents, as well as provide Display names for existing Onshape properties. Administrators can add, modify and retire properties for all users. Users can only view these metadata definitions.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Categories
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Categories
topics.desc: Create categories in Onshape to extend the properties of the standard Onshape object types in the system to include more targeted and relevant metadata to be applied based on design, engineering, and manufacturing processes.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Items
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Items
topics.desc: Add items that you will want to add to your bill of materials but that do not require being modeled (non-geometric entities). Adding those items here allows you to make use of them in any company/enterprise-owned documents.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Applications
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Applications
topics.desc: Access and manage third-party applications for use with your Onshape Professional, Educator, or Enterprise subscription.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Numbering Schemes
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Numbering Schemes
topics.desc: Select manual or sequential number generation for release objects (parts, Assemblies, drawings, files), standard content, and items.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Release Management
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Release Management
topics.desc: Select from a set of automated workflows in Onshape used to manage releasing revisions of parts, Assemblies, Drawings and imported files (translated or not) in a document.

topics.title: Enterprise Settings - Task Management
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Task Management
topics.desc: Allows Enterprise admins to manage task workflows. Enterprise admins can activate, deactivate, unpublish, and set default task workflows for the Enterprise.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Preferences
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Preferences
headings: Date type format and Export rules
topics.desc: Select your Onshape Preferences settings, where you have the ability to require that users use approved drawing templates, make use of company/classroom/enterprise-owned material libraries in their own accounts, or show a view only toolbar to all users of a document with view only permissions, as well as additional preference settings.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Revision Tools
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Revision Tools
topics.desc: Change the part number type of released objects to allow for part number reuse bewteen types (i.e., parts, assemblies, and drawings).

topics.title: Enterprise Settings - Integrations
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Integrations
topics.desc: Available to Enterprise administrators only; grant or remove access to Cloud storage integrations and integration users, and set up Collaboration integrations, such as Slack.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Webhooks
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Webhooks
topics.desc: Administrators can use webhooks to check data access integrity, ensuring that a notification was really sent by Onshape, and that it has not been tampered with in transit. Enabling webhook basic authentication populates the Authorization header in all webhook requests.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Developer
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Developer
topics.desc: Allow Enterprise admins to create new apps to which Enterprise users can subscribe. Admins can manage and distribute these apps to specified users.

topics.title: Enterprise Settings - Arena
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Arena
topics.desc: Grant or remove access to Microsoft OneDrive, Dropbox, and Google Drive accounts to Onshape.

topics.title: Enterprise Settings - Job Queue
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Job Queue
topics.desc: Provides a list of all Arena PLM BOM and Release candidate sync jobs and their statuses.

topics.title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Details
topics.path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Details
topics.desc: View and update the details of the company/classroom/enterprise information and change the logo image.

topics.title: Account Menu
topics.path: Account Menu > Inactive Onshape Account Policy
topics.desc: An inactive Onshape account is an account that has not been used (logged into) during the past 4 years. Inactive accounts are deleted after 4.5 years.

topics.title: Managing Your Onshape Account And Subscription
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
headings: Managing Your Onshape Account And Subscription
topics.desc: Onshape offers different types of accounts based on different levels of need regarding data management and collaboration requirements: Enterprise, Professional, Standard, Education, and Free.

topics.title: Subscriptions and Payment FAQs
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Subscriptions and Payment FAQs
topics.desc: This topic covers Plan Faq, outlining subscriptions and payment questions and answers.

topics.title: Free Account
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Free Subscription
topics.desc: This topic covers how to manage your Onshape free subscription.

topics.title: Student Subscription
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Student Subscription
topics.desc: Student subscriptions are for degree- or certificate-seeking students at accredited education institutions. This plan is solely for classroom instruction, student learning projects, school clubs or organizations, and academic research. This plan is not for government, commercial, or other organizational use.

topics.title: Standard Subscription
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Standard Subscription
topics.desc: Standard subscriptions are directed towards single professional users who do not have a need for company-wide settings and functionality. Standard subscriptions are billed per user (at an annual rate of $1,500), and include all Onshape features with the exception of the following: Automated Release management tools, Custom properties (company metadata), Company-wide material libraries, Company-based sharing, and Consolidated billing.

topics.title: Managing Your Onshape Professional Trial
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Professional Trial
topics.desc: A Professional Trial, available from a Free or Standard subscription, allows you to try out all the features of a Professional subscription, and then transition to a Professional subscription once the trial is over.

topics.title: Professional Subscription
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Professional Subscription
topics.desc: The Onshape Professional subscription enables you to consolidate billing for multiple users, thereby creating a Company within Onshape: a named, user-visible Onshape entity with consolidated billing, ownership and sharing for a set of Professional subscription users.

topics.title: Managing Your Onshape Educator Subscription
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription
headings: Managing Your Onshape Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription
All users are migrated to the new subscription
Classroom-owned documents are migrated to the new account
Transfer any non-classroom-owned documents or folders
topics.desc: Educator subscriptions are for current faculty members or volunteers at accredited education institutions, and provides access to Classes and Assignments. This plan is solely for classroom instruction, organizations, and academic research. This plan is not for government, commercial, or other organizational use.

topics.title: Educator Concepts and Terminology
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Concepts and Terminology
topics.desc: This topic covers the terms and concepts to help provide a foundation for understanding and using Onshape Educator subscription.

topics.title: Educator Interface
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Interface
headings: Assigning a Student Educator status for a class
topics.desc: This topic explains the Educator user interface.

topics.title: Educator Classes
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Classes
topics.desc: This topic explains how to administer Educator classes.

topics.title: Educator Assignments
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Assignments
topics.desc: This topic explains how to administer Educator assignments.

topics.title: EDU Enterprise Dashboards
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription > EDU Enterprise Dashboards
topics.desc: Available dashboards in the EDU Enterprise plan and the information contained therein.

topics.title: Enterprise Subscription
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription
topics.desc: Onshape Enterprise is Onshape’s premium product offering designed for sophisticated product teams who need to work fast without losing control of data.

topics.title: Getting Started as an Enterprise User
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise User
headings: Getting Started as an Enterprise User
topics.desc: When working within an Enterprise in Onshape, be aware that you are in a separate, managed environment that has a subtle difference from other types of Onshape subscriptions. The Enterprise environment is owned and managed by an Enterprise Administrator and can include many users, called Members of the Enterprise. All users belonging to a specific Enterprise plan access Onshape through a single URL, specifically for their Enterprise.

topics.title: Getting Started as a Light User
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as a Light User
headings: Getting Started as a Light User
topics.desc: Light user accounts are typically used by members of the internal supply chain, managers or executives, and can even be provided to external suppliers or clients. All Onshape users have access to the one single source of their enterprise data.

topics.title: Getting Started as an Enterprise Administrator
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin
headings: Getting Started as an Enterprise Administrator
topics.desc: As an Enterprise Administrator, you are responsible for defining permissions for users. You have, by default, full access and full permission to your company’s resources. Optionally, you are able to grant similar permissions to other users using Global permissions.

topics.title: Two-factor Authentication for Enterprise
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Two-factor Authentication for Enterprise
topics.desc: As the Admin of an Enterprise, you decide whether or not to require two-factor authentication use by company members. In the Company/Enterprise settings, you can configure your company's single sign-on and require two-factor authentication for Enterprise members.

topics.title: Project Roles and Permission Schemes
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Project Roles and Permission Schemes
topics.desc: Project roles and Permission schemes work in tandem to apply access permission to documents grouped together within a Project. A Project references only one Permission scheme, which is comprised of Project roles specifying the permissions.

topics.title: Managing Projects
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Managing Projects
topics.desc: Projects enable you to group documents and apply permissions to those documents for individual users and groups of users (called Teams). The permissions are assigned at the Project level through the association of a Permission scheme along with the specification of a role map (one per Project) that contains a list of user/role pairs. (The user may be an individual user or a Team of users.)

topics.title: Integrating with Identity Providers
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Integrating with Identity Providers
topics.desc: Before starting the integration process, you must have requested, and been approved for, an Onshape Enterprise account or trial, and have an Onshape Enterprise domain name.

topics.title: Integrating with Okta
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Integrating with Identity Providers > Integrating with Okta
topics.desc: This section covers how to set up and integrate Onshape with Okta single sign-on (SSO).

topics.title: Integrating with OneLogin
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Integrating with Identity Providers > Integrating with OneLogin
topics.desc: This section covers how to set up and integrate Onshape with OneLogin single sign-on (SSO).

topics.title: Setting Up Single Sign On with Google
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Integrating with Identity Providers > Setting Up Single Sign On with Google
headings: Setting up Single Sign On with Google
topics.desc: This section covers how to set up and integrate Onshape with Google single sign-on (SSO).

topics.title: Integrating with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD)
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Integrating with Identity Providers > Integrating with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD)
headings: Integrating with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD)
topics.desc: This section covers how to set up and integrate Onshape with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) single sign-on (SSO).

topics.title: Microsoft ADFS
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
topics.path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Integrating with Identity Providers > Integrating with Microsoft ADFS
topics.desc: This section covers how to set up and integrate Onshape with Microsoft ADFS single sign-on (SSO).

topics.title: Integrating with PingOne
topics.section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
